      "observations": [
        "All five owned paths and every changed hunk were read. The landing adds a zero-initialized shared mLockedFlags field, early returns in ClearFlag and ToggleFlag, and preservation of the mask in SetFlags. The accepted source retains these operations; the existing ClearFlag database-ownership lesson is reused only for its bounded current method scope.",
        "ClearFlag and ToggleFlag return NS_OK for the whole operation when any input-mask bit intersects mLockedFlags. They do not selectively modify the unlocked portion of a compound mask. SetFlags ORs all locked bits into its requested value. The new tests exercise single-bit calls, not mixed locked/unlocked masks.",
        "The original SetBoxFlags starts newFlags from mFlags, adds protocol-derived flags, then assigns mLockedFlags = newFlags & SpecialUse before SetFlags. The accepted function has the same combined-mask dataflow. Thus the mask can include a pre-existing SpecialUse bit; it is not computed from isolated newly advertised bits alone. The inspected discovery caller sets Trash from a protocol flag before SetBoxFlags. Arbitrary user-setting reachability, later reconnection and a runtime defect are not established.",
        "The new mock IMAP test discovers folders before adding its unlocked test bits. It directly checks locked Inbox, SentMail, Drafts, Trash, Junk and Archive plus unlocked Unused4 and ordinary-folder SentMail/Archive. It does not directly cover Queue, Templates, compound masks or a local SpecialUse bit set before later SetBoxFlags. All nine assertion call sites have nonempty expected-result messages; missing should alone is not a patch defect.",
        "The sole author inline says locking occurs only after connection/discovery and describes changing settings earlier as unlikely. That belief is not a source invariant. Reviewer feedback asks to share the mask and three base methods; the owned implementation does so. Later multiple-folder reports remain historical reports, separate from these static contracts.",
        "Complete Root primary c43e0790e7826315fc7e6c97ebd63c7f0714491cea9bf1672c9e2697bce06628 retains all current comments 0–12. It records disagreement about server/client flag separation, correction of a one-patch test report after both patches were applied, and later persistent multiple/protected-folder reports. These reports do not establish that this landing cures every case.",
        "D306647 asks for a shared base mask and flag methods; those operations are present. Its sole author inline qualifies the pre-discovery timing assumption rather than proving that account settings cannot precede discovery. Later reported multiple Sent icons remain distinct from the static combined-mask finding and from the added single-bit tests."
